ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Williams, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Failure to pass meconium since birth and poor feeding

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient presents to the emergency department later the same day following an earlier outpatient pediatric evaluation, brought by his concerned parents. The pregnancy was full-term with no complications, and the delivery was vaginal without any perinatal issues. The mother reports that the baby has had bilious vomiting since the first day of life.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Hirschsprung disease (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

ALLERGIES:
None known

FAMILY HISTORY:
- No known family history of Hirschsprung disease or other congenital bowel disorders

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: None. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Newborn.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the neonate appears lethargic with a distended abdomen. Rectal examination reveals increased rectal tone and explosive passage of stool upon withdrawal of the examining finger.

IMAGING:
Abdominal radiography shows dilated bowel loops with a transition zone in the rectosigmoid area.

attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Pediatrics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Failure to pass meconium since birth

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
A 2-day-old male infant is brought to the pediatrician by his concerned parents due to failure to pass meconium since birth. The full-term infant was delivered vaginally without complications. The mother reports that the infant has been feeding poorly and has had episodes of bilious vomiting.

ALLERGIES:
None known

FAMILY HISTORY:
- No known family history of Hirschsprung disease or other congenital bowel disorders

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: None. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Newborn.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the infant appears lethargic with a distended abdomen. Rectal examination reveals tight anal sphincter tone and explosive release of stool and gas upon digital rectal examination.

IMAGING:
Abdominal radiography shows a dilated colon proximal to a transition zone and absence of air in the distal rectum.
